intent.raw_query: Greece under $2000, beaches and local food, summer, flying from NYC

experiences.name: Sunrise Swim at Elafonissi Beach
experiences.description: Visit the famous pink-sand Elafonissi Beach in Crete at sunrise to enjoy the shallow turquoise lagoons and stunning colors before the midday heat sets in. The unique pink hue comes from crushed shells and coral. Spend the morning snorkeling and wading through the shallow waters. Retreat to a nearby taverna for shade and refreshments by late morning.

experiences.name: Athens Central Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the historic Varvakios Agora (Athens Central Market) in the cooler morning hours. Sample local cheeses, olives, cured meats, fresh seafood, and traditional Greek pastries like spanakopita and bougatsa. Chat with local vendors and learn about Greek culinary traditions. This indoor-friendly market is a perfect alternative on hot or rainy days, offering an authentic taste of everyday Greek life.

experiences.name: Evening Meze Dinner in Thessaloniki's Ladadika District
experiences.description: As the sun sets and temperatures cool, head to the vibrant Ladadika neighborhood for a traditional Greek meze dinner. Order a spread of grilled octopus, saganaki (fried cheese), tzatziki, dolmades, and fresh bread paired with local ouzo or tsipouro. Thessaloniki is considered Greece's food capital, and this lively district offers dozens of authentic tavernas with outdoor seating perfect for a breezy evening meal.

experiences.name: Sunset Catamaran Cruise around Santorini Caldera
experiences.description: Board a small-group catamaran in the late afternoon to sail around the volcanic Santorini caldera. Swim in the warm Aegean Sea at volcanic hot springs, snorkel over lava formations, and watch the world-famous Santorini sunset from the water. A light Greek dinner with wine is typically included on board. The evening timing avoids the intense midday heat while offering the most spectacular lighting for photos.

experiences.name: Indoor Greek Cooking Class in Heraklion
experiences.description: Join a hands-on cooking class held in a traditional Cretan kitchen, ideal for avoiding midday heat or rainy weather. Learn to prepare authentic Cretan dishes such as dakos (barley rusk salad), lamb with stamnagathi greens, and loukoumades (honey doughnuts). The instructor sources ingredients from local markets and explains the history and health benefits of the Mediterranean diet. You'll enjoy eating everything you cook as a full meal at the end.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Greece
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 14:50
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Athens International Airport (Eleftherios Venizelos) at 14:50. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take the X95 express bus or Metro Line 3 into central Athens — both budget-friendly options under €10. Check into your budget hostel or guesthouse in the Monastiraki or Psiri neighborhood.
day_by_day.evening: Take a relaxed evening stroll through Monastiraki Square and the Plaka neighborhood. Admire the illuminated Acropolis from street level. Grab a cheap souvlaki wrap from a street vendor to kick off your Greek food experience.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or grab a coffee and tiropita (cheese pie) at the airport
meals.lunch: Snack at the airport or on arrival — grab a spanakopita from a bakery near the metro
meals.dinner: Souvlaki wrap from a street kiosk in Monastiraki (€2–3) — try Kostas or Thanasis for authentic cheap eats

day_by_day.notes: Buy an Ath.ena reloadable transit card at the airport metro station for discounted bus and metro fares throughout your Athens stay. Exchange a small amount of cash for tips and market purchases.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Acropolis early (opens at 8:00 AM) to beat the heat and crowds. Explore the Parthenon, Erechtheion, and Propylaea. Combined ticket (~€20) includes several nearby sites — worth every cent. Bring water and sunscreen.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk down to the Ancient Agora of Athens (included in the combined ticket). Explore the well-preserved Temple of Hephaestus and the Stoa of Attalos museum. Afterward, wander through the Monastiraki flea market for budget souvenirs and people-watching.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Psiri neighborhood for dinner. Explore the lively tavernas and ouzeries. Enjoy a budget mezze spread with locals.

meals.breakfast: Greek yogurt with honey and walnuts from a nearby bakery or mini-market (€2–3)
meals.lunch: Gyros or souvlaki plate from a local grill near Monastiraki (€4–6)
meals.dinner: Mezze dinner at a Psiri taverna — order shared plates of tzatziki, dolmades, and grilled vegetables (€8–12 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The combined Acropolis ticket is valid for 5 days and covers 7 archaeological sites — keep it safe. Wear comfortable walking shoes as the Acropolis hill is steep and uneven.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the National Archaeological Museum (one of the world's greatest — entry ~€10). Spend 2–3 hours exploring ancient Greek artifacts, the Antikythera Mechanism, and stunning bronze statues.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take the metro to the Panathenaic Stadium (Kallimarmaro) — free to view from outside or €5 to enter. Then stroll through the upscale Kolonaki neighborhood and up Lycabettus Hill for panoramic views of Athens (free hike or funicular ~€7 round trip).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Plaka for dinner. Explore the charming narrow streets and enjoy a sit-down meal at one of the affordable traditional restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Bougatsa (custard-filled pastry) and coffee at a local kafeneio (€3–4)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from a bakery — cheese pie, olive bread, and fresh juice (€4–5)
meals.dinner: Traditional moussaka or pastitsio at a Plaka taverna (€9–13 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The National Archaeological Museum is closed on Mondays — check the schedule. Lycabettus Hill at sunset offers one of the best free views in Athens.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early KTEL bus from Athens (Kifissos Bus Terminal) to Nafplio — a scenic 2.5-hour ride (~€14 one way). Arrive and check into a budget guesthouse. Drop your bags and head to the old town.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Nafplio's charming Venetian old town on foot. Visit Syntagma Square, browse local shops, and climb the 999 steps to the impressive Palamidi Fortress (€8 entry) for sweeping views over the Argolic Gulf.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the waterfront promenade at sunset. Enjoy the relaxed atmosphere of this romantic coastal town.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and koulouri (sesame bread ring) before the bus departure in Athens (€2)
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood or grilled fish at a harbor-side taverna in Nafplio (€10–14)
meals.dinner: Budget dinner at a local psistaria (grill house) — lamb chops or chicken with salad and bread (€10–12)

day_by_day.notes: Book the KTEL bus ticket in advance during summer. Nafplio is a great base for exploring the Peloponnese. The Palamidi climb is strenuous — go early or late afternoon to avoid midday heat.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Ancient Mycenae (~30 min by local bus or taxi, ~€12 entry). Explore the Lion Gate, Treasury of Atreus (Tomb of Agamemnon), and the ancient citadel. A UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of Greece's most important Bronze Age sites.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Nafplio and spend the afternoon at Arvanitia Beach — a small, free pebble beach just a 10-minute walk from the old town. Swim in the clear Aegean waters and relax in the afternoon sun (avg 23°C — perfect beach weather).
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a leisurely evening in Nafplio's old town. Browse the boutiques and settle in for a long Greek dinner.

meals.breakfast: Greek coffee and tiropita at a kafeneio in Nafplio (€3)
meals.lunch: Packed picnic from the local market — olives, feta, bread, tomatoes (€5–6)
meals.dinner: Fresh grilled octopus and Greek salad at a waterfront taverna (€12–15)

day_by_day.notes: Arvanitia Beach has a small café and changing facilities. Bring your own snorkeling gear if possible — the water is crystal clear. Mycenae is best visited in the morning before tour groups arrive.

day_by_day.morning: Take the KTEL bus from Nafplio to Athens (Kifissos Terminal), then connect to Piraeus Port. Board a budget ferry to Santorini (Thira) — book in advance with Hellenic Seaways or Blue Star Ferries (~€35–50 for a deck/economy seat, ~8 hours). Enjoy the scenic Aegean crossing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Santorini at Athinios Port. Take the local bus (€1.80) to Fira (the capital). Check into a budget hostel or studio apartment in Fira or nearby Karterados village (cheaper than Oia).
day_by_day.evening: Explore Fira on foot — walk along the caldera rim path, browse the local shops, and enjoy your first Santorini sunset.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the Nafplio bus station café before departure (€3–4)
meals.lunch: Packed food or ferry snack bar on board (€5–8)
meals.dinner: Budget gyros or souvlaki in Fira town — avoid the overpriced caldera-view restaurants (€6–8)

day_by_day.notes: Book ferry tickets well in advance for June travel — Santorini is extremely popular. Overnight ferries save on accommodation costs if you prefer. The local KTEL bus on Santorini is very affordable and connects all major villages.

day_by_day.morning: Take the local bus to Oia village (€1.80) and explore its iconic blue-domed churches, white-washed buildings, and narrow alleyways in the cooler morning hours. Visit the Venetian Castle ruins.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Perissa or Perivolos Beach on the south coast by local bus (€1.80). These black volcanic sand beaches are free and lined with budget beach bars. Swim, sunbathe, and enjoy the unique landscape.
day_by_day.evening: Stay at Perissa for sunset or return to Fira. Grab dinner at one of the affordable tavernas in Perissa village — much cheaper than Fira or Oia.

meals.breakfast: Fresh bread, local honey, and coffee at a Fira bakery (€3–4)
meals.lunch: Beach taverna lunch at Perissa — grilled fish or a Greek salad with pita (€8–11)
meals.dinner: Taverna dinner in Perissa village — fresh calamari, tzatziki, and local wine (€10–13)

day_by_day.notes: Oia gets extremely crowded at sunset — arrive early or enjoy the sunset from a less crowded spot. Perissa and Perivolos beaches have free public access areas alongside paid sunbed sections.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a scooter or ATV (€15–25/day) to explore Santorini independently. Start with Ancient Akrotiri — a remarkably preserved Minoan Bronze Age city buried by volcanic ash (~€12 entry). One of the most important prehistoric sites in the Aegean.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Red Beach (Kokkini Paralia) near Akrotiri — a dramatic beach with red and black volcanic cliffs. Short hike required (10 min). Then visit White Beach (accessible by water taxi from Red Beach, ~€5). Swim and snorkel in the clear waters.
day_by_day.evening: Return scooter and head to Fira for the evening. Walk the caldera path from Fira toward Imerovigli for stunning views. Enjoy a budget dinner back in Fira.

meals.breakfast: Greek yogurt parfait and coffee at a Fira café (€4–5)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from a mini-market — local cheese, olives, bread, and fruit (€5–6)
meals.dinner: Affordable taverna in Fira's back streets — avoid the caldera-view premium (€10–13)

day_by_day.notes: Red Beach can be rocky and requires water shoes. Scooter rental requires a valid license in Greece. Akrotiri is covered and air-conditioned — a great midday activity to escape the heat.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early ferry from Santorini to Mykonos (Blue Star or SeaJets, ~2–3 hours, ~€30–45). Arrive and check into a budget hostel in Mykonos Town (Chora). Drop bags and explore the iconic windmills and Little Venice neighborhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Paradise Beach or Paraga Beach by local bus or water taxi (~€2–5). These are Mykonos's most famous beaches — enjoy the turquoise water and lively atmosphere. Public areas are free; sunbeds are optional.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Mykonos Town for the evening. Explore the maze-like whitewashed alleys of Chora, find the famous Petros the Pelican, and enjoy the vibrant atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast on the ferry or at the Santorini port café (€3–5)
meals.lunch: Gyros or souvlaki wrap in Mykonos Town — budget options exist away from the tourist strip (€4–6)
meals.dinner: Affordable taverna dinner in the back streets of Chora — fresh fish soup or grilled chicken (€10–14)

day_by_day.notes: Mykonos is one of Greece's pricier islands — stick to back-street restaurants and self-catering where possible. Book accommodation well in advance. The local bus (KTEL) is the cheapest way to reach beaches.

day_by_day.morning: Take a short boat trip to the sacred island of Delos (~€20 round trip including entry). One of the most important archaeological sites in Greece — birthplace of Apollo and Artemis. Explore the ancient ruins, mosaics, and the famous Terrace of the Lions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Mykonos and spend the afternoon at Agios Sostis Beach — a quieter, free beach on the north coast accessible by local bus. No sunbeds or beach bars — just natural beauty and calm waters.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks at a budget bar in Mykonos Town (happy hour deals available). Enjoy the famous Mykonos nightlife atmosphere without overspending.

meals.breakfast: Spanakopita and Greek coffee at a Chora bakery (€3)
meals.lunch: Packed picnic on Delos or at Agios Sostis — buy supplies from a mini-market (€5–6)
meals.dinner: Souvlaki plate or gyros at a budget grill in Mykonos Town (€7–9)

day_by_day.notes: Delos boats depart from the Old Port of Mykonos Town — check schedules as they are limited. Bring plenty of water and sun protection for Delos as there is almost no shade. Agios Sostis is one of the few truly unspoiled beaches on Mykonos.

day_by_day.morning: Take a ferry back to Athens (Piraeus) from Mykonos — book in advance (~€35–50, 2.5–5 hours depending on ferry type). Arrive in Athens and check back into a budget hostel in the city center.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Benaki Museum of Greek Culture (~€9 entry) or the free Museum of Greek Folk Art in Plaka. Explore the Thissio neighborhood and the Kerameikos archaeological site (€8, included in combined ticket if still valid).
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Athens — revisit your favorite neighborhood or explore somewhere new. Head to Exarchia neighborhood for a more local, bohemian Athens experience with affordable bars and restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Ferry café or pack your own snacks for the journey (€3–5)
meals.lunch: Falafel wrap or gyros near Monastiraki on arrival (€4–6)
meals.dinner: Dinner in Exarchia — try a local taverna for home-style Greek cooking at very affordable prices (€8–11)

day_by_day.notes: If your combined Acropolis ticket is still valid (issued within 5 days), use it at Kerameikos. Exarchia is a vibrant, authentic neighborhood popular with students and locals — very budget-friendly.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Cape Sounion by KTEL bus from Athens (Pedion Areos bus stop, ~€7 each way, 1.5 hours). Visit the stunning Temple of Poseidon perched on a cliff above the sea (~€10 entry). Arrive early for the best light and fewer crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Swim at the small beach below Cape Sounion or at Legrena Beach nearby (free). Enjoy the crystal-clear water and dramatic coastal scenery. Return to Athens by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Final shopping for souvenirs at the Monastiraki flea market. Enjoy a farewell dinner in Athens with your favorite Greek dishes.

meals.breakfast: Koulouri and coffee from a street vendor near the bus stop (€2–3)
meals.lunch: Packed picnic at Cape Sounion — buy supplies from an Athens mini-market before departure (€5–6)
meals.dinner: Farewell Greek feast — order a spread of mezze, grilled meat, and local wine at a Psiri or Monastiraki taverna (€12–16)

day_by_day.notes: The KTEL bus to Sounion runs along the coastal road (more scenic) or the inland road — take the coastal route for beautiful sea views. Sunset at the Temple of Poseidon is legendary but very crowded — the morning visit is more peaceful.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Athens — enjoy a leisurely Greek breakfast at a local café. Take a last walk through Plaka or Monastiraki. Visit any remaining sites or do last-minute souvenir shopping at the central market (Varvakios Agora) for local products like olive oil, herbs, and honey.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Athens International Airport via Metro Line 3 from Monastiraki or Syntagma (~€10, 40 minutes). Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your departure flight for check-in and security.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Athens — carry the memories of 13 incredible days exploring Greece's history, beaches, and food culture!

meals.breakfast: Full Greek breakfast — eggs, feta, olives, tomatoes, and coffee at a Plaka café (€6–8)
meals.lunch: Light meal or snack at the airport — or grab a final souvlaki near the metro station before heading to the airport (€4–6)
meals.dinner: Airport dining or on the flight

day_by_day.notes: Pack any liquid food souvenirs (olive oil, honey, wine) in checked luggage. Keep receipts for VAT refund eligibility on purchases over €50. The Athens Metro to the airport is the most reliable and budget-friendly airport transfer option.

trip_options.title: Classic Greece Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

experiences.name: Sunrise Swim at Elafonissi Beach
experiences.description: Visit the famous pink-sand Elafonissi Beach in Crete at sunrise to enjoy the shallow turquoise lagoons and stunning colors before the midday heat sets in. The unique pink hue comes from crushed shells and coral. Spend the morning snorkeling and wading through the shallow waters. Retreat to a nearby taverna for shade and refreshments by late morning.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 14:50
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Athens International Airport (Eleftherios Venizelos) at 14:50. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take the X95 express bus or Metro Line 3 to central Athens. Check in to your mid-range hotel in the Monastiraki or Koukaki neighborhood. Freshen up and take a gentle orientation stroll around Monastiraki Square and the Ancient Agora area to get your bearings.
day_by_day.evening: Wander through the atmospheric Plaka neighborhood — Athens' oldest district with neoclassical architecture and winding pedestrian lanes. Enjoy a relaxed first dinner at a traditional taverna on a quiet side street.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight or airport)
meals.lunch: Grab a quick gyros wrap or spanakopita from a street kiosk near the airport or upon arrival in central Athens (€4–7)
meals.dinner: Taverna To Kafeneio or similar Plaka taverna — try moussaka, tzatziki, and a glass of house wine (€18–25 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light given the afternoon arrival. Keep luggage light for the metro ride. Validate your metro ticket before boarding. Exchange some cash or use ATMs in the airport arrivals hall.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning visit to the Acropolis (open from 8:00 AM) — arrive by 8:15 AM to beat the crowds and midday heat. Explore the Parthenon, Erechtheion, and Propylaea. Descend to visit the Acropolis Museum, one of the finest archaeological museums in Europe, housing original friezes and artifacts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the vibrant Monastiraki Flea Market for browsing local crafts, vintage goods, and souvenirs. Walk through Ermou Street toward Syntagma Square to watch the Evzone guards change at the Hellenic Parliament (on the hour). Explore the National Garden for a shaded afternoon break.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Thissio or Psyrri neighborhood for dinner — both are lively with outdoor seating and great people-watching. Enjoy a sunset view of the Acropolis lit up from a rooftop bar.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a neighborhood bakery — koulouri (sesame bread ring) and Greek coffee (€4–6)
meals.lunch: Souvlaki at Monastiraki — Thanasis or Bairaktaris are iconic spots (€8–12)
meals.dinner: Taverna in Psyrri neighborhood — grilled octopus, Greek salad, and local Assyrtiko white wine (€20–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book Acropolis tickets online in advance at e-ticketing.gr to avoid queues. Combined ticket (€30) covers multiple archaeological sites. Wear comfortable shoes — cobblestones are uneven. Sunscreen essential at 23°C.

day_by_day.morning: Take the early morning ferry from Piraeus Port (30-min metro from central Athens) to the island of Aegina — a short 1-hour ferry ride. Visit the remarkably preserved Temple of Aphaia, one of Greece's best-preserved ancient temples, set on a pine-covered hill with panoramic views.
day_by_day.evening: Return ferry to Piraeus by early evening. Dinner in Athens' Koukaki neighborhood — a local, less touristy area beloved by Athenians.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Aegina Town's charming harbor front lined with colorful fishing boats and neoclassical buildings. Rent a bicycle or take a local bus to the fishing village of Perdika for a swim at the clear, calm beach. Sample Aegina's famous pistachios — the island is Greece's pistachio capital.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at hotel before heading to Piraeus — yogurt with honey and fruit
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch at a harbor taverna in Perdika village — grilled fish of the day with horta (wild greens) (€15–22 per person)
meals.dinner: Mezze dinner in Koukaki, Athens — dolmades, saganaki, and taramasalata with pita (€16–22 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Ferries from Piraeus to Aegina run frequently (every 1–2 hours). Conventional ferry ~€9 each way; Flying Dolphin hydrofoil ~€16 each way. Bring cash for smaller island vendors. Pistachio shopping is a must — buy directly from local producers.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Athens by domestic flight or ferry to Crete (Heraklion). Flight is approximately 45 minutes; ferry overnight option also available but flight recommended for time efficiency. Upon arrival, pick up a rental car (pre-booked, ~€35–45/day) — essential for exploring Crete independently. Drive to Heraklion city center and check in to your hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the magnificent Palace of Knossos — the legendary Minoan palace complex dating back 3,500 years, just 5km from Heraklion. Explore the reconstructed frescoes, throne room, and labyrinthine corridors. Afterward, visit the Heraklion Archaeological Museum to see the original Minoan artifacts including the famous Phaistos Disc.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Heraklion's lively Lion Square (Plateia Venizelou) and the 16th-century Morosini Fountain. Stroll along the Venetian harbor and the impressive Koules Fortress at sunset.

meals.breakfast: Airport or hotel breakfast — Greek yogurt parfait with local thyme honey
meals.lunch: Quick bite near Knossos — local bakery or café serving Cretan dakos (barley rusk with tomato and feta) (€6–9)
meals.dinner: Traditional Cretan restaurant near Lion Square — lamb with stamnagathi (wild greens), Cretan cheese platter, and local Vidiano wine (€22–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book Knossos tickets online to skip queues (€15 entry). Rental car is strongly recommended for Crete — public transport is limited outside cities. June weather in Crete is warm and sunny — perfect beach conditions ahead. Keep hotel receipts for car rental drop-off coordination.

day_by_day.morning: Drive west from Heraklion along the scenic E75 coastal highway toward Rethymno (1.5 hours). Stop at the beautiful Bali beach village for a morning swim in crystal-clear turquoise coves — a hidden gem with multiple small beaches tucked between rocky headlands.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Rethymno — one of Crete's most charming towns with a perfectly preserved Venetian old town. Explore the narrow alleyways, the impressive Fortezza castle overlooking the sea, and the Venetian lighthouse. Browse the covered market street for local products.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy dinner in Rethymno's atmospheric old town. The harbor front is lined with excellent seafood restaurants with romantic evening ambiance.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast in Heraklion before departing
meals.lunch: Beachside snack at Bali — fresh fruit, local cheese pie (tiropita), and cold Mythos beer (€8–12)
meals.dinner: Seafood taverna on Rethymno harbor — grilled sea bream, shrimp saganaki, and Cretan rosé wine (€22–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Bali village is best visited on weekday mornings before crowds arrive. Rethymno old town is a UNESCO-listed area — wear comfortable walking shoes on the cobblestones. Consider staying overnight in Rethymno to explore the evening atmosphere.

day_by_day.morning: Drive the spectacular E65 road through the White Mountains (Lefka Ori) toward Chania — Crete's most beautiful city. Stop at the Agia Triada Monastery for a peaceful morning visit surrounded by olive groves and mountain scenery. Arrive in Chania and check in to your accommodation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Chania's stunning Venetian harbor — arguably the most photogenic spot in all of Crete. Visit the covered market (Agora) for local cheeses, olives, herbs, and honey. Walk through the Splantzia and Topanas neighborhoods with their mix of Venetian, Ottoman, and Greek architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks at a harbor-front café watching the lighthouse glow golden. Dinner in the old town — Chania has some of Crete's finest restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast in Rethymno before departing — Cretan honey pie (melopita) and Greek coffee
meals.lunch: Chania Agora market lunch — assemble a picnic of local cheeses, olives, cured meats, and fresh bread (€10–14)
meals.dinner: Upscale-casual restaurant in Chania old town — slow-cooked lamb with artichokes, Cretan graviera cheese, and local Dafnes red wine (€25–32 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Chania is widely considered Crete's most beautiful city — allow extra time to simply wander. The covered market is closed Sunday afternoons. Book dinner reservations in advance for popular harbor-front restaurants on weekends.

day_by_day.morning: **Featured Experience — Sunrise Swim at Elafonissi Beach:** Wake at 5:00 AM and drive 1.5 hours southwest to the legendary Elafonissi Beach. Arrive at sunrise (approximately 6:10 AM in late June) to experience the famous pink-sand beach and shallow turquoise lagoon in near-total solitude. The pink hue comes from crushed coral and shells — most vivid in morning light. Wade through the warm, knee-deep lagoon to the small island of Elafonissi for panoramic views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the late morning and early afternoon enjoying Elafonissi — swimming, snorkeling in the clear waters, and relaxing on the pink sand before day-trippers arrive in numbers. Drive back toward Chania via the scenic coastal road, stopping at Falasarna Beach — a long, wide sandy beach with excellent swimming and dramatic cliff backdrops.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Chania for a relaxed evening. Visit the Firkas Fortress and the Naval Museum. Enjoy a leisurely dinner at a traditional Cretan mezedopoleio (meze restaurant).

meals.breakfast: Pack a pre-prepared breakfast the night before — energy bars, fruit, and a thermos of coffee for the early sunrise drive
meals.lunch: Beach taverna at Elafonissi or Falasarna — fresh calamari, Greek salad, and cold drinks (€14–18 per person)
meals.dinner: Mezedopoleio in Chania — share 6–8 small plates including fava, grilled halloumi, and Cretan sausage (€18–24 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Elafonissi is one of Greece's most popular beaches — arriving at sunrise is essential for the magical, crowd-free experience. Bring a flashlight for the pre-dawn drive on mountain roads. The lagoon is very shallow (knee-deep) and safe for all swimmers. Apply sunscreen before the sun rises — UV is intense even in early morning.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to the Samaria Gorge trailhead at Xyloskalo (1 hour from Chania). Hike the famous Samaria Gorge — Europe's longest gorge at 16km, descending through dramatic limestone cliffs, ancient forests, and the iconic Iron Gates (narrowest point, just 3 meters wide). The hike takes 4–6 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Emerge at the coastal village of Agia Roumeli at the bottom of the gorge. Cool off with a well-deserved swim in the Libyan Sea — the water here is exceptionally clear and refreshing after the hike. Take the ferry from Agia Roumeli to Hora Sfakion (45 minutes), then bus back to Chania.
day_by_day.evening: Rest and recovery evening in Chania. Light dinner and early night after the demanding hike.

meals.breakfast: Early hearty breakfast before the hike — eggs, bread, cheese, and fruit at hotel or nearby café
meals.lunch: Pack a trail lunch — sandwiches, nuts, dried fruit, and plenty of water (2+ liters essential)
meals.dinner: Light taverna dinner near your Chania hotel — grilled chicken souvlaki, village salad, and fresh bread (€14–18 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Samaria Gorge entry fee: €5. The gorge is one-way (top to bottom only). Wear proper hiking shoes — the rocky terrain is demanding. Start early (gates open at 7:00 AM) to avoid midday heat. The gorge is closed in winter and after heavy rain. Ferry from Agia Roumeli: ~€12. This is a full, physically demanding day — rest well the night before.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed recovery morning in Chania. Sleep in, enjoy a leisurely breakfast, and visit the Chania Archaeological Museum housed in a beautiful Venetian church. Browse the leather goods shops on Skridlof Street (famous for handmade sandals and bags).
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive east along the northern coast to the beautiful Marathi Beach near Akrotiri Peninsula — a quiet, locals-favorite sandy beach with calm, clear water and a handful of excellent fish tavernas. Spend the afternoon swimming and relaxing.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Chania for a final evening. Visit the rooftop bar at a boutique hotel for panoramic views of the old town and harbor at dusk. Farewell dinner in Chania.

meals.breakfast: Extended hotel breakfast or neighborhood café — Cretan breakfast platter with local honey, thyme, rusks, and soft cheese (€8–12)
meals.lunch: Fish taverna at Marathi Beach — grilled whole fish by the kilo, octopus, and cold Cretan beer (€18–25 per person)
meals.dinner: Upscale Cretan cuisine restaurant in Chania old town — slow-roasted pork with local herbs, kritharoto (Cretan orzo), and aged Cretan wine (€28–35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Marathi Beach is a local secret — relatively uncrowded even in June. The fish tavernas here are excellent value and authenticity. Today is intentionally relaxed after yesterday's demanding gorge hike. Use the afternoon to recharge before the next travel day.

day_by_day.morning: Return rental car at Chania Airport and take a short domestic flight to Santorini (Thira Airport). Alternatively, take a high-speed ferry from Heraklion to Santorini (2 hours). Check in to your accommodation in Fira or Imerovigli — both offer stunning caldera views at mid-range prices compared to Oia.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Fira — Santorini's vibrant capital perched on the caldera rim. Walk the caldera-edge path from Fira toward Firostefani and Imerovigli (2.5km, stunning views). Visit the Museum of Prehistoric Thera to see artifacts from the ancient Akrotiri civilization buried by the volcanic eruption.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the famous Santorini sunset — while Oia is the most famous spot, the caldera path between Imerovigli and Skaros Rock offers equally spectacular views with fewer crowds. Dinner with caldera views.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before travel — hotel or airport café
meals.lunch: Quick lunch in Fira after check-in — gyros or a café sandwich while exploring (€8–12)
meals.dinner: Caldera-view restaurant in Fira or Imerovigli — fresh tuna carpaccio, fava santorinis (yellow split pea purée), and local Assyrtiko wine (€28–38 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Santorini is the most expensive Greek island — budget accordingly (€30–45/person for dinner is typical at caldera-view restaurants). Book accommodation well in advance for June. Fira and Imerovigli offer better value than Oia while maintaining stunning views. The caldera walking path is one of the world's great walks — do it at golden hour.

day_by_day.morning: Take the local bus or rent an ATV/scooter to explore the island. Visit the ancient site of Akrotiri — a remarkably preserved Bronze Age city buried by volcanic ash around 1600 BC, often called the 'Minoan Pompeii.' The site is covered and air-conditioned — perfect for a morning visit.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Perissa or Perivolos Beach on the island's south coast — Santorini's famous black volcanic sand beaches. The dark sand absorbs heat, so bring sandals. Swim in the clear Aegean, rent a sunbed, and enjoy the lively beach bar atmosphere. The contrast of black sand, blue sea, and white cliffs is uniquely Santorinian.
day_by_day.evening: Drive or bus to Oia village for the legendary sunset (arrive by 7:00 PM to secure a good spot — it gets very crowded). After sunset, enjoy dinner in Oia's quieter back streets away from the main tourist drag.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or local bakery — tiropita and freddo cappuccino (Greek iced coffee) (€5–8)
meals.lunch: Beach taverna at Perissa — fresh seafood pasta, Greek salad, and cold Mythos beer (€16–22 per person)
meals.dinner: Taverna in Oia's back streets — stuffed tomatoes (Santorini specialty), white eggplant, and local wine (€24–32 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Akrotiri entry: €12. ATV/scooter rental: €25–35/day — useful for island flexibility but drive carefully on narrow roads. Perissa beach sunbed rental: €8–12 for two. Oia sunset is world-famous but extremely crowded — arrive early and consider the Skaros Rock viewpoint near Imerovigli as a less-crowded alternative.

day_by_day.morning: Morning boat tour of the Santorini caldera — depart from Fira's old port (accessible by cable car or donkey path). Visit the active volcanic island of Nea Kameni, hike to the crater, and swim in the warm sulfuric hot springs at Palea Kameni. Continue to the picturesque village of Thirassia — the quieter, less-visited sister island with authentic local life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Santorini by early afternoon. Spend the afternoon at Kamari Beach — a more relaxed black-sand beach with a long promenade, water sports, and good beach bars. Alternatively, visit the hilltop ancient site of Ancient Thera for panoramic island views.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening on Santorini — enjoy a special dinner at a slightly splurge-worthy restaurant. Santorini's local specialties (fava, white eggplant, cherry tomatoes, capers) are unique to the volcanic soil and worth celebrating on the last island night.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before the boat tour — hotel breakfast or quick café stop
meals.lunch: Lunch on Thirassia island — simple, authentic taverna with fresh fish and local wine away from tourist crowds (€16–20 per person)
meals.dinner: Special farewell dinner at a caldera-view restaurant — Santorini fava with capers, grilled lobster pasta, and a bottle of Sigalas Assyrtiko (€35–50 per person, slight splurge for the occasion)

day_by_day.notes: Caldera boat tours: €25–40 per person depending on operator and inclusions. Book through your hotel or at the old port. The hot springs are a highlight — bring an old swimsuit as the sulfur can stain. Thirassia is a wonderful contrast to tourist-heavy Santorini — genuinely local and peaceful.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning on Santorini — enjoy a slow breakfast and last caldera views. Pack and check out. Take a final walk along the caldera path or browse local shops for last-minute gifts: local wine, saffron, capers, and fava are excellent Santorini souvenirs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer to Santorini Airport (Thira) for return flight to Athens, then onward connection. Alternatively, if departing from Athens, take the high-speed ferry to Piraeus (4.5–5 hours) and transfer to Athens airport. Allow ample time for connections.
day_by_day.evening: Departure or overnight in Athens if needed for an early next-day flight. If time permits, a final dinner at Athens airport or a quick souvlaki near Syntagma Square.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely final Greek breakfast — yogurt with Santorini honey, fresh fruit, and strong Greek coffee (€8–12)
meals.lunch: Light airport lunch or ferry snacks — Greek salad, cheese pie, and water
meals.dinner: Airport dinner or quick Athens souvlaki if transiting — gyros wrap and cold drink (€8–12)

day_by_day.notes: Santorini Airport is small and gets very busy in summer — arrive 2 hours before domestic flights, 2.5 hours for international. Duty-free at Santorini airport has good local wine selections. Confirm all onward flight connections before departure day. Keep one set of clean clothes accessible in carry-on for the journey home. Total trip highlights: Athens archaeology, Aegina island day trip, Crete's beaches and gorge, Elafonissi sunrise, and Santorini's iconic caldera — a perfectly balanced Greek experience.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Greece Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Sunrise Swim at Elafonissi Beach
experiences.description: Visit the famous pink-sand Elafonissi Beach in Crete at sunrise to enjoy the shallow turquoise lagoons and stunning colors before the midday heat sets in. The unique pink hue comes from crushed shells and coral. Spend the morning snorkeling and wading through the shallow waters. Retreat to a nearby taverna for shade and refreshments by late morning.

experiences.name: Athens Central Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the historic Varvakios Agora (Athens Central Market) in the cooler morning hours. Sample local cheeses, olives, cured meats, fresh seafood, and traditional Greek pastries like spanakopita and bougatsa. Chat with local vendors and learn about Greek culinary traditions. This indoor-friendly market is a perfect alternative on hot or rainy days, offering an authentic taste of everyday Greek life.

experiences.name: Evening Meze Dinner in Thessaloniki's Ladadika District
experiences.description: As the sun sets and temperatures cool, head to the vibrant Ladadika neighborhood for a traditional Greek meze dinner. Order a spread of grilled octopus, saganaki (fried cheese), tzatziki, dolmades, and fresh bread paired with local ouzo or tsipouro. Thessaloniki is considered Greece's food capital, and this lively district offers dozens of authentic tavernas with outdoor seating perfect for a breezy evening meal.

experiences.name: Sunset Catamaran Cruise around Santorini Caldera
experiences.description: Board a small-group catamaran in the late afternoon to sail around the volcanic Santorini caldera. Swim in the warm Aegean Sea at volcanic hot springs, snorkel over lava formations, and watch the world-famous Santorini sunset from the water. A light Greek dinner with wine is typically included on board. The evening timing avoids the intense midday heat while offering the most spectacular lighting for photos.

experiences.name: Indoor Greek Cooking Class in Heraklion
experiences.description: Join a hands-on cooking class held in a traditional Cretan kitchen, ideal for avoiding midday heat or rainy weather. Learn to prepare authentic Cretan dishes such as dakos (barley rusk salad), lamb with stamnagathi greens, and loukoumades (honey doughnuts). The instructor sources ingredients from local markets and explains the history and health benefits of the Mediterranean diet. You'll enjoy eating everything you cook as a full meal at the end.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 14:50
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Athens International Airport Eleftherios Venizelos at 14:50 on Air Serbia. Clear customs, collect luggage, and transfer via private luxury car service to your five-star hotel in central Athens (e.g., Hotel Grande Bretagne or Electra Metropolis). Check in, freshen up, and enjoy a welcome drink on the rooftop terrace overlooking the Acropolis.
day_by_day.evening: Take a leisurely stroll through the charming Plaka neighborhood — Athens' oldest district — to shake off travel fatigue. Admire the illuminated Acropolis from below before settling in for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Served on the plane or at the airport lounge
meals.lunch: Not applicable (in transit)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Strofi Restaurant in Plaka — a legendary Athens taverna with a rooftop terrace offering stunning Acropolis views. Enjoy classic Greek dishes such as lamb kleftiko, grilled octopus, and fresh tzatziki paired with a fine Assyrtiko white wine.

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance. Request an Acropolis-view room at check-in if available. Keep Day 1 light to recover from travel.

day_by_day.morning: Athens Central Market Food Tour — Head to the historic Varvakios Agora (Athens Central Market) in the cool morning hours. Join a guided premium food tour to sample local cheeses, cured meats, olives, spices, fresh seafood, and traditional street foods. Engage with local vendors and learn about Greek culinary heritage in one of Athens' most vibrant and authentic spaces.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Acropolis and Parthenon with a private expert guide, avoiding the peak midday crowds by timing entry around 13:00–14:00. Explore the Acropolis Museum afterward for world-class exhibits on ancient Greek civilization in a beautifully air-conditioned setting.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a sunset cocktail at a rooftop bar in Monastiraki (e.g., A for Athens rooftop bar) with panoramic Acropolis views, then head to dinner.

meals.breakfast: Lavish buffet breakfast at your hotel — fresh pastries, Greek yogurt with Cretan honey, seasonal fruits, and eggs cooked to order
meals.lunch: Light mezedes lunch at a traditional ouzeri near the Central Market — try taramosalata, spanakopita, and grilled sardines with ouzo
meals.dinner: Dinner at Varoulko Seaside (Piraeus) or Spondi (Athens) — both Michelin-starred restaurants offering elevated modern Greek cuisine with exceptional wine lists

day_by_day.notes: Book Acropolis tickets and private guide in advance. The food tour typically lasts 3–4 hours. Wear comfortable walking shoes and light clothing.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the ancient Agora of Athens and the Temple of Hephaestus with your private guide, then wander through the upscale Kolonaki neighborhood. Visit the Benaki Museum for a curated look at Greek art and history spanning thousands of years.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer to Athens International Airport for a short domestic flight to Heraklion, Crete (approximately 45 minutes). Check in to your luxury hotel in Crete (e.g., Domes Noruz Chania or Caramel Boutique Resort). Spend the afternoon relaxing by the infinity pool overlooking the Aegean Sea.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Venetian harbor of Heraklion on foot, visiting the iconic Koules Fortress at dusk as the golden light reflects off the water.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — Greek yogurt parfait, honey-drizzled loukoumades, fresh-squeezed orange juice, and a selection of local cheeses
meals.lunch: Quick but quality lunch at a harbor-side taverna in Heraklion — fresh grilled fish, Cretan dakos salad, and a glass of local Vidiano wine
meals.dinner: Dinner at Peskesi Restaurant in Heraklion — a celebrated farm-to-table Cretan restaurant sourcing ingredients from their own organic farm. Try the slow-cooked lamb with stamnagathi greens and aged graviera cheese.

day_by_day.notes: Book domestic flight Athens–Heraklion well in advance. Arrange private transfer from Heraklion Airport to your hotel. Pack a smaller bag for the Crete leg of the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Indoor Greek Cooking Class in Heraklion — Join a hands-on premium cooking class held in a traditional Cretan kitchen. Learn to prepare authentic dishes such as dakos, boureki, kalitsounia (Cretan cheese pies), and a classic lamb stew using locally sourced ingredients. The class includes a market visit to select fresh produce.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Palace of Knossos — the legendary Minoan palace complex — with a private archaeologist guide. Explore the labyrinthine ruins, vibrant frescoes, and learn about Europe's oldest civilization in depth.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel for a relaxing sunset swim in the infinity pool, followed by a private in-room or terrace dining experience arranged by the hotel's concierge.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — Cretan rusk with tomato and olive oil, local honey, fresh fruit platter, and strong Greek coffee
meals.lunch: Enjoy the dishes you prepared during the cooking class as part of the experience — a true farm-to-table feast
meals.dinner: Private terrace dinner at your luxury hotel or at Avli Restaurant in Rethymno (if day-tripping) — renowned for its romantic garden setting and refined Cretan cuisine

day_by_day.notes: The cooking class typically runs 4–5 hours including the market visit. Book Knossos private guide separately. Knossos is best visited in the afternoon when tour groups thin out.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise Swim at Elafonissi Beach — Depart early (around 05:30) by private car for the 1.5-hour drive to the legendary Elafonissi Beach on Crete's southwest coast. Arrive at sunrise to experience the famous pink-sand shores and shallow turquoise lagoon in near-total solitude. Swim in the crystal-clear waters as the sun rises over the Aegean — an utterly magical and exclusive experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the late morning and early afternoon relaxing on Elafonissi Beach before the crowds arrive. Explore the small island accessible by wading through the shallow lagoon. Begin the return drive to your hotel, stopping at a traditional Cretan village en route for refreshments.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Heraklion or Chania. Enjoy a relaxing evening with a spa treatment at your hotel (massage, hammam, or thalassotherapy) before a late dinner.

meals.breakfast: Pack a premium picnic breakfast prepared by your hotel the night before — fresh pastries, fruit, yogurt, and coffee in a thermos to enjoy on the beach at sunrise
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch at a family-run taverna near Elafonissi or Paleochora village — grilled sea bream, fried calamari, and village salad
meals.dinner: Dinner at Thalassino Ageri in Chania — a romantic seafood restaurant perched on the rocks above the sea, serving exceptional fresh fish and Cretan specialties

day_by_day.notes: Depart no later than 05:30 to reach Elafonissi by sunrise (approximately 06:00 in June). Bring sunscreen, a hat, and water. The beach gets very crowded by mid-morning — early arrival is essential for the premium experience.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the enchanting old town of Chania — one of Greece's most beautiful Venetian-era cities. Wander through the narrow alleyways, visit the covered market, and admire the lighthouse and Venetian harbor. Browse artisan shops for local olive oil, herbs, and handmade leather goods.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a private boat excursion from Chania harbor to the secluded Balos Lagoon and Gramvousa Island. Swim in the impossibly blue waters of Balos — a UNESCO-protected lagoon with white sand and shallow turquoise sea. Enjoy snorkeling and sunbathing in complete luxury.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Chania for a relaxed evening. Stroll the illuminated Venetian harbor at dusk and enjoy cocktails at a waterfront bar.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a charming café in Chania's old town — fresh tiropita, Cretan honey pie, Greek coffee, and fresh orange juice
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet lunch on the private boat to Balos — prepared by your hotel or a local deli: local cheeses, charcuterie, olives, bread, and chilled white wine
meals.dinner: Dinner at Ela Restaurant in Chania old town — a beloved local institution serving traditional Cretan recipes with a modern twist in a beautiful stone-walled setting

day_by_day.notes: Book the private boat to Balos in advance — a private charter is far superior to the crowded ferry. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, snorkeling gear, and plenty of water. Balos is one of Crete's crown jewels.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Crete via a short domestic flight from Heraklion or Chania to Santorini (Thira Airport). Check in to your clifftop luxury hotel in Oia or Imerovigli (e.g., Canaves Oia Epitome, Grace Hotel Santorini, or Andronis Luxury Suites). Settle in and enjoy your private plunge pool with caldera views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the iconic village of Oia on foot — wander through the blue-domed churches, whitewashed cave houses, and art galleries. Visit the Oia Castle ruins for panoramic caldera views. Browse high-end boutiques for local jewelry, ceramics, and art.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a pre-dinner cocktail on your private terrace as the sun begins to set over the caldera — one of the world's most celebrated sunsets. Dine at a clifftop restaurant with unobstructed caldera views.

meals.breakfast: In-flight snack or airport lounge breakfast; upon arrival, enjoy a welcome fruit platter and champagne at your hotel
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a cliffside café in Oia — fresh Greek salad, grilled halloumi, and a glass of Santorini's famous Assyrtiko wine
meals.dinner: Dinner at Lauda Restaurant at Andronis Luxury Suites — a Michelin-recommended restaurant with breathtaking caldera views, serving refined Mediterranean cuisine with premium local ingredients

day_by_day.notes: Oia gets extremely crowded at sunset — your hotel terrace or a private sunset experience is far more enjoyable than the castle viewpoint crowds. Book dinner reservations well in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Take a private guided tour of Santorini's volcanic landscape — visit the ancient site of Akrotiri (the 'Pompeii of the Aegean'), a remarkably preserved Minoan Bronze Age settlement buried by a volcanic eruption. Explore with a private archaeologist for an in-depth experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the famous Red Beach near Akrotiri for a swim and sunbathe session. The dramatic red volcanic cliffs create a surreal and stunning backdrop. Alternatively, visit the black-sand Perissa Beach for a more relaxed afternoon with beach club amenities.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset Catamaran Cruise around the Santorini Caldera — board a small-group or private catamaran in the late afternoon to sail around the volcanic caldera. Swim in hot springs, snorkel in crystal-clear waters, and watch the legendary Santorini sunset from the sea. Enjoy onboard BBQ, fresh salads, and unlimited local wine and cocktails.

meals.breakfast: Lavish hotel breakfast on your private terrace — eggs Benedict, smoked salmon, Greek yogurt with Santorini cherry tomatoes, fresh pastries, and freshly brewed coffee
meals.lunch: Beachside lunch at a taverna near Red Beach — grilled octopus, fresh fish, and a cold Mythos beer or glass of Vinsanto
meals.dinner: Gourmet BBQ dinner served onboard the catamaran as you sail the caldera at sunset — fresh grilled fish, Greek salads, local cheeses, and fine Santorini wines

day_by_day.notes: Book a private catamaran charter for the most exclusive experience — avoid large group tours. Akrotiri requires advance ticket booking. Red Beach involves a short rocky walk — wear appropriate footwear.

day_by_day.morning: Spend a leisurely morning at your hotel — enjoy a late breakfast, a dip in your private plunge pool, and a spa treatment (volcanic stone massage or wine therapy treatment, a Santorini specialty). Take in the extraordinary caldera views at your own pace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Santorini's renowned wineries for a premium wine tasting experience. Tour Santo Wines or Domaine Sigalas — two of the island's most prestigious producers. Learn about the unique basket-vine cultivation method used on the island and taste exceptional Assyrtiko, Nykteri, and Vinsanto wines paired with local cheeses and charcuterie.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the capital Fira — visit the Museum of Prehistoric Thera and browse the upscale shops along the caldera-edge promenade. Enjoy a final Santorini dinner with caldera views.

meals.breakfast: Extended hotel breakfast — a leisurely affair with all the Greek classics plus freshly made waffles, smoked salmon, and a Bloody Mary or fresh juice
meals.lunch: Gourmet wine-paired lunch at the winery — artisan cheeses, local honey, fava dip, and Santorini's famous cherry tomato bruschetta alongside premium wine tastings
meals.dinner: Dinner at Selene Restaurant in Pyrgos — one of Santorini's most acclaimed restaurants, celebrating local Cycladic ingredients with sophisticated modern Greek cuisine and an extraordinary wine cellar

day_by_day.notes: Book winery tours in advance, especially for Domaine Sigalas which has limited capacity. The spa at luxury Santorini hotels often requires advance booking — arrange upon check-in.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Santorini via ferry or short flight to Thessaloniki, Greece's vibrant second city and culinary capital. Check in to your luxury hotel (e.g., Makedonia Palace or Excelsior Hotel). Freshen up and head out to explore the city's UNESCO-listed Byzantine monuments.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the White Tower — Thessaloniki's iconic landmark — and stroll along the beautiful waterfront promenade. Explore the Rotunda, the Arch of Galerius, and the Byzantine walls. Visit the Archaeological Museum of Thessaloniki for world-class Macedonian gold artifacts.
day_by_day.evening: Evening Meze Dinner in Thessaloniki's Ladadika District — As the sun sets and temperatures cool, head to the vibrant Ladadika neighborhood for a traditional Greek meze experience. This former warehouse district is now Thessaloniki's most atmospheric dining quarter, filled with tavernas and ouzeris. Enjoy an extended feast of small plates — grilled loukaniko sausage, smoked eggplant, fresh mussels, and more — accompanied by ouzo or tsipouro.

meals.breakfast: In-transit — airport or ferry lounge; light snack on arrival
meals.lunch: Lunch at a traditional bougatsa shop in Thessaloniki — the city's famous custard-filled pastry — followed by a proper sit-down meal at a local taverna near the waterfront
meals.dinner: Extended meze dinner in Ladadika — visit Zythos or Aristotelous Square area restaurants for the finest Thessaloniki meze experience with premium local wines and spirits

day_by_day.notes: Thessaloniki is considered Greece's food capital — embrace the local dining culture of long, leisurely meals. The ferry from Santorini to Piraeus takes 8+ hours; a short flight is recommended for comfort.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the extraordinary ancient site of Vergina — the royal tombs of the Macedonian kings, including Philip II (father of Alexander the Great). This UNESCO World Heritage Site houses one of Greece's most spectacular archaeological museums, built within the actual burial mounds. A private guide will bring the history to life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Thessaloniki and explore the vibrant Modiano and Kapani covered markets — a sensory feast of spices, fresh produce, seafood, and local delicacies. Visit the Museum of Byzantine Culture, a world-class institution with stunning mosaics and artifacts.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a sunset walk along Thessaloniki's famous waterfront, stopping at the iconic Umbrellas sculpture. Attend a live rebetiko music performance at a traditional venue — rebetiko is Thessaloniki's soulful urban folk music, a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — fresh bougatsa, Greek yogurt with local honey, seasonal fruit, and strong Greek coffee (Thessaloniki is famous for its coffee culture)
meals.lunch: Lunch at a premium seafood restaurant near the Thessaloniki waterfront — fresh grilled fish, seafood pasta, and chilled Malagousia white wine
meals.dinner: Dinner at Extravaganza or Clochard Restaurant — among Thessaloniki's finest dining establishments, offering refined Greek cuisine with exceptional local wine selections in elegant surroundings

day_by_day.notes: Vergina is approximately 75 km from Thessaloniki — arrange a private car and guide. The museum is built underground within the burial mounds and is remarkably well-preserved. Book in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the extraordinary monasteries of Meteora — one of Greece's most breathtaking UNESCO World Heritage Sites. Dramatic sandstone rock pillars rise hundreds of meters above the Thessaly plain, topped by ancient Byzantine monasteries. Depart early by private car (approximately 3 hours from Thessaloniki). Visit the most impressive monasteries — Great Meteoron and Varlaam — with a private guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Meteora — hike between monasteries on scenic footpaths with stunning views of the rock formations and surrounding valley. Visit the Holy Trinity Monastery (famously featured in the James Bond film 'For Your Eyes Only'). Enjoy the extraordinary landscape as afternoon light transforms the rocks.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Thessaloniki (or overnight in Kalambaka near Meteora for a more relaxed pace). Enjoy a quiet, celebratory penultimate evening dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before departure — packed to go if needed
meals.lunch: Lunch at a traditional taverna in Kalambaka village at the base of Meteora — hearty Greek mountain cuisine including lamb chops, horta (wild greens), and local red wine
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at your Thessaloniki hotel's signature restaurant or at Aristotelous Square — a grand setting for a celebratory final evening meal with premium Greek wines

day_by_day.notes: Meteora is a long but absolutely unmissable day trip. Modest dress is required to enter the monasteries (shoulders and knees covered). Some monasteries are closed on certain days — check schedules in advance. Consider overnighting in Kalambaka to reduce driving.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Greece — enjoy a leisurely breakfast at your hotel and take a last stroll along Thessaloniki's waterfront promenade. Visit any remaining sites or shops for last-minute souvenirs: premium Greek olive oil, saffron from Kozani, local wines, or handmade jewelry.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of your hotel and transfer by private car to Thessaloniki Macedonia International Airport (SKG) for your return flight to Belgrade on Air Serbia. Alternatively, if flying from Athens, take a domestic connection. Enjoy the airport lounge before departure.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — carry home extraordinary memories of pink-sand beaches, volcanic sunsets, ancient ruins, and the finest flavors of Greek cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Final luxurious hotel breakfast — savor every last bite of Greek yogurt, local honey, fresh pastries, and strong Greek coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the airport lounge or a quick farewell meal at a quality restaurant near the hotel before checkout
meals.dinner: In-flight or upon return home

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before departure for airport check-in and security. Purchase any duty-free Greek products at the airport — Santorini wines, Mastiha liqueur, and Greek olive oil make excellent gifts. Confirm return flight details with Air Serbia in advance.

query: Greece under $2000, beaches and local food, summer, flying from NYC
